chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Abi Nasr, from Abd al-Karim, from al-Halabi, who said:
I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife while she is menstruating. So he said: 'A divorce contrary to the Sunnah is invalid.'

key_terms.الطلاق لغير السنة: Divorce contrary to the Sunnah — a divorce that does not meet the prescribed legal conditions (e.g., pronounced during menstruation or multiple pronouncements at once)
key_terms.باطل: Invalid, void, null — has no legal effect
key_terms.حائض: A woman in the state of menstruation (hayd)

ai.seo_question: Is a divorce pronounced during menstruation valid in Shia Islam?
ai.summary: Al-Halabi narrates that he asked Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) about a man who divorces his wife during her menstrual period. The Imam gave the authoritative ruling that such a divorce, which violates the conditions set by the Sunnah, is null and void. This ruling reflects the Islamic legal principle that divorce during menstruation (talaq al-bid'ah) is prohibited, as it contravenes both the Quran (65:1) and established prophetic practice.
